```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(p8105.datasets)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)

data("instacart", package = "p8105.datasets")

# Each original row represents one product in an order.
aisle_df = instacart |>
  count(aisle, name = "n_items") |>
  slice_max(n_items, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE)

# Create one row per order to avoid counting orders multiple times.
order_df = instacart |>
  group_by(order_id) |>
  summarise(
    order_hour_of_day = first(order_hour_of_day),
    order_dow = first(order_dow),
    basket_size = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

hour_df = order_df |>
  count(order_hour_of_day, name = "n_orders")

order_df = order_df |>
  mutate(
    day_code = factor(order_dow, levels = 0:6)
  )

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 14))
```

Row {data-height=180}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### About this dashboard

This dashboard explores the Instacart dataset from the `p8105.datasets`
package. Each original row represents a product in an order. Order-level
summaries use one record per order, and basket size is the number of product
records in that order.

The plots show the ten most frequently purchased aisles, orders by hour,
and basket size by day-of-week code. Day codes are displayed as 0–6
without assuming named weekdays.

Hover over plots to inspect values, drag to zoom, and double-click to reset.

[Return to homepage](index.html)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Top 10 aisles by number of items purchased

```{r aisle_bar}
aisle_plot = aisle_df |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = reorder(aisle, n_items),
    y = n_items
  )) +
  geom_col(fill = "#377EB8") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(
    x = "Aisle",
    y = "Number of items purchased"
  )

ggplotly(aisle_plot)
```

Row {data-height=450}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Number of orders by hour of day

```{r hourly_line}
hour_plot = hour_df |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = order_hour_of_day,
    y = n_orders
  )) +
  geom_line(color = "#377EB8", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(color = "#377EB8", size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 23, by = 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(
    x = "Hour of day (0–23)",
    y = "Number of orders"
  )

ggplotly(hour_plot)
```

### Distribution of basket size by day-of-week code

```{r basket_boxplot}
plot_ly(
  data = order_df,
  x = ~day_code,
  y = ~basket_size,
  type = "box",
  boxpoints = FALSE,
  color = I("#377EB8")
) |>
  layout(
    xaxis = list(title = "Day-of-week code (0–6)"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Number of products per order"),
    showlegend = FALSE
  )
```
